newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF falls as 9-mo figures disappoint.
newsitem.headline: BASF falls as 9-mo figures disappoint.

text.p: Shares in German chemical company BASF AG fell on Wednesday as its nine month figures disappointed the market, coming in under expectations, dealers said.
The group reported an 8.8 percent rise in group nine-month pre-tax profits to 3.37 billion marks but said third quarter pre-tax profits slipped 2.3 percent to 1.05 billion marks.
In pre-bourse electronic dealings, BASF was down over two percent or 1.15 marks to 51.32 marks by 0847 GMT, having earlier fallen to 51 marks.
After the utility Veba, BASF was morning's the most heavily traded stock, 700,000 shares changing hands.
Meanwhile the rest of the market was slightly firmer, with the IBIS DAX index up 3.79 points, or 0.14 percent at 2,768.09 points, having earlier risen to an all-time high of 2,772.29.

BASF AG said it expected full-year 1996 sales to show a three percent rise and pre-tax profits to be at least as high as year-ago levels, but some traders said that had not been enough to encourage the stock.
